title: Reject non-finite derived proficiency-testing scores
prompt:
Prevent a synthetic proficiency-testing event from passing with an infinite calculated standard deviation. Change only lib/ohworks-pt-scoring.ts and add tests/ohworks-pt-derived-overflow.test.ts. Evidence: lib/ohworks-pt-scoring.ts:338-345 calculates standardDeviation from high-low without checking the derived result, then divides by it to classify participants. A reproduced declared consensus with assignedValue=0 and acceptableRange={low:-1e308,high:1e308}, participant reportedValue=1e308, minSatisfactoryRate=1, and maxUnsatisfactoryCount=0 returns standardDeviation=Infinity, zScore=0, and outcome=pass. The quality-indicators demo renders these calculated statistics and event outcomes.

Enforce finite assigned values, finite strictly positive derived standard deviations, and finite participant z-scores before producing a scored result. Cover both declared-consensus and robust-statistics paths. Use PtScoringError with a dedicated sanitized derived-statistics error code when arithmetic cannot produce valid statistics; preserve the existing zero-spread and malformed-input errors. Do not silently replace invalid numbers with zero or publish partial participant scores.

Test the reproduced range overflow, robust-statistic arithmetic overflow, z-score arithmetic overflow, and ordinary finite controls. Assert the exact typed error and unchanged valid classifications. Run node --import tsx --test tests/ohworks-pt-derived-overflow.test.ts. Planner reproduction confirmed the false pass; all 140 tests across the six relevant existing suites passed. Open and recently merged PR diffs were checked for duplication. work on the assigned branch you are on. Keep this a two-file, synthetic-only change with no external operations.
